title: Yoneda splicing respects equivalence and annihilates a zero prefix
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. A degree-$r$ Yoneda extension of $U$ by $V$, for $r\geq1$, means an exact sequence $0\to V\to X_{r-1}\to\cdots\to X_0\to U\to0$. Equivalence means the relation generated by morphisms of these sequences fixing both endpoints. Fix a short exact sequence $\sigma:0\to K\xrightarrow{i}P\xrightarrow{q}F\to0$ and an integer $m\geq1$. For an $m$-extension $\eta:0\to T\to X_{m-1}\to\cdots\to X_0\xrightarrow{d}K\to0$, its splice with $\sigma$ is the exact $(m+1)$-extension $0\to T\to X_{m-1}\to\cdots\to X_0\xrightarrow{i\circ d}P\xrightarrow{q}F\to0$. Splicing with $\sigma$ preserves Yoneda equivalence. If $\eta$ is Yoneda equivalent to the zero $m$-extension of $K$ by $T$, its splice is Yoneda equivalent to the zero $(m+1)$-extension of $F$ by $T$. Here the zero $1$-extension is $0\to T\to T\oplus K\to K\to0$ with the standard inclusion and projection. For $r\geq2$, the zero $r$-extension of $U$ by $V$ has first middle object $V$, last middle object $U$, $r-2$ intervening zero objects, identity arrows at the endpoints, and zero arrows between middle objects. No projective or injective objects are assumed.
